questions.question: Q1 During the simulation, which parameter had the greatest influence on the projected junction depth?

explanations.a: Ion dose mainly controls dopant concentration.
explanations.b: Correct! Implantation energy determines how deeply ions penetrate into the silicon wafer.
explanations.c: Wafer diameter remains constant throughout the process.
explanations.d: Vacuum pressure allows ion travel but does not directly determine junction depth.

questions.question: Q2 Increasing the ion dose during implantation primarily results in:

explanations.a: Correct! A higher ion dose implants more dopant atoms into the wafer.
explanations.b: Junction depth is mainly controlled by implantation energy.
explanations.d: Ion dose and implantation energy are independent parameters.

questions.question: Q3 Which output parameter directly indicates how far the implanted ions have penetrated into the silicon wafer?

explanations.a: Sheet resistance depends on dopant concentration.
explanations.b: Uniformity describes how evenly ions are distributed.
explanations.c: Correct! Junction depth measures the penetration depth of implanted ions.
explanations.d: Device quality is an overall performance indicator.

questions.question: Q4 Which combination of process parameters generally produced the highest device quality during the simulation?

answers.a: Very low energy and very low dose
answers.b: Moderate implantation energy and recommended ion dose
answers.c: Highest possible energy and longest implantation time

explanations.a: Very low values usually result in insufficient doping.
explanations.b: Correct! Operating within the recommended parameter range produces the best implantation quality.
explanations.c: Extremely high values may introduce excessive lattice damage.
explanations.d: Random values rarely produce optimum results.

questions.question: Q5 Which dopant selected in the simulation produces a P-type semiconductor region?

explanations.c: Correct! Boron is the standard P-type dopant.

questions.question: Q6 Why is beam scanning performed during ion implantation?

answers.b: To ensure uniform dopant distribution across the wafer surface

explanations.a: Cooling is not the purpose of beam scanning.
explanations.b: Correct! Beam scanning provides uniform implantation over the entire wafer.
explanations.c: Wafer thickness does not change during implantation.
explanations.d: Scanning does not affect implantation energy.

questions.question: Q7 Which output parameter is most directly affected by changes in ion dose?

explanations.a: Correct! Increasing dopant concentration generally decreases sheet resistance.
explanations.c: Crystal orientation is fixed during wafer fabrication.

questions.question: Q8 Which process step must be completed before starting ion implantation in the simulation?

explanations.a: Correct! The ion source, magnetic analyzer, and accelerator must be prepared before implantation begins.
explanations.b: The wafer must remain inside the chamber.
explanations.d: Metal deposition is a different fabrication process.

questions.question: Q9 What is the purpose of the acceleration column in an ion implanter?

answers.b: To accelerate ions to the required implantation energy
answers.c: To remove dopants from the wafer

explanations.a: The acceleration column does not cool ions.
explanations.b: Correct! It accelerates ions using a high-voltage electric field before implantation.
explanations.c: Ion implantation introduces dopants rather than removing them.
explanations.d: Silicon dioxide is grown during oxidation.

questions.question: Q10 Based on the simulation, the highest device quality is achieved when:

answers.a: Recommended implantation energy, ion dose, and implantation time are maintained
answers.b: The highest possible implantation energy is always selected
answers.d: The lowest ion dose is used

explanations.a: Correct! Maintaining the recommended operating conditions produces the best junction formation and overall device quality.
explanations.b: Very high energy may damage the crystal lattice.
explanations.c: Time alone does not ensure optimum implantation.
explanations.d: Very low ion dose results in insufficient doping.
